name: AL
notes: Aluminum metal fuel. Typical particle size 5 micron (spherical). Common loads 10-20 wt%.

name: HTPB
notes: R-45M HTPB binder. Hf = -2.97 kcal/mol. Weq = 1190.5 g/eq (hydroxyl equivalent weight).

name: IDP
notes: Isodecyl pelargonate plasticizer. Hf = -209.5 kcal/mol. Reduces mixture viscosity. Typical 2-4 wt%.

name: AP_CUSTOM
notes: Ammonium perchlorate oxidizer. Hf = -70.69 kcal/mol. Standard particle sizes: 400, 200, 90, 30 micron. Typical load 60-80 wt%.

name: HMDI
notes: Hydrogenated MDI curative. Hf = -75.27 kcal/mol. Cures HTPB. NOTE: Weq not set - add measured value for cure calculator.

name: RIO
notes: Red iron oxide (Fe2O3) burn rate catalyst. Hf = -197.3 kcal/mol. Typical load 0.1-1 wt%. Produces yellow flame, decreases pot life.

name: IPDI
notes: IPDI isocyanate curative. Hf = -88.8 kcal/mol. Weq = 111 g/eq. Slower cure time, longer pot life than PAPI/E744. Moisture sensitive.

name: DOA
notes: Dioctyl adipate plasticizer. Reduces mixture viscosity. Typical 2-4 wt%.

name: CASTOR_OIL
notes: Castor oil crosslinking agent. Weq = 164 g/eq (hydroxyl). Increases crosslink density and propellant strength. Requires additional curative.

name: BIO
notes: Black iron oxide (Fe3O4) burn rate catalyst. Produces yellow flame.

name: CUO
notes: Black copper oxide burn rate catalyst. Blue/violet flame. Typical load 1-2 wt%.

name: OXAMIDE
notes: Oxamide burn rate suppressant. 1-6 wt% (beyond that makes prop hard to ignite). Reduction in Isp. Can stabilize combustion instability.

name: TEPANOL_HX878
notes: Tepanol HX-878 bonding agent. Weq ~211 g/eq (hydroxyl). Bonds AP to binder. VERY TOXIC. Typically ~1 wt%. High viscosity - requires long mixing. No CEA formula available.

name: DBTDL
notes: DBTDL cure catalyst. Speeds up curing. Added by the drop - dilute 10x or 100x with plasticizer. Overnight cure possible. No CEA formula available - weight-track only.

name: TPB
notes: Triphenyl Bismuth. Dual role: cure catalyst (with 7-day cure) and cure rate modifier for TMO catalysts. Increases pot life when used with MgO. No CEA formula available.
